seoTitle: Stripe Instant Payouts: Setup, Eligibility & Fees
metaDescription: Enable Stripe Instant Payouts: the exact eligibility checks, the real fee by country (1% or 1.5%, not a vague percentage), the 10-per-day cap, and why it isn't always a debit card.
intro:
Instant Payouts move your Stripe balance to a payout method in minutes, typically within 30 minutes, instead of the usual multi-day payout cycle. Stripe doesn't turn the feature on for everyone automatically, and it isn't available in every country Stripe supports.

This guide walks through where the eligibility checks live in your dashboard, the exact fee and per-payout limits Stripe's documentation lists, and the daily cap that catches people who assume Instant Payouts has no ceiling.
prerequisites: A Stripe account in a country where Instant Payouts is supported (the US, Canada, UK, most of the EU, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Hong Kong, and a handful of others; not every Stripe country is included)
A complete, verified business profile in the Stripe Dashboard
An eligible payout method added: a debit card in most supported countries, or in a few (including the US, UK, EU, Sweden, Denmark, Australia, Singapore and Hong Kong) certain bank accounts instead
costNote: Stripe charges 1% per Instant Payout in Canada, the EU, UK, Singapore, Norway, Hong Kong and Malaysia, and 1.5% in the US, Australia, New Zealand and UAE. The fee is deducted from the payout itself. A standard payout on your default schedule has no equivalent fee.

steps.heading: Sign in to your Stripe dashboard
steps.body: Instant Payouts is managed entirely from your live Stripe dashboard, so the first step is logging in with the account tied to the payments you want to speed up. If you manage more than one Stripe account, confirm you're on the right one. Payout method and eligibility are account-specific and don't carry over between accounts.

image.caption: The Stripe sign-in screen. Payout settings live inside the account you log into here, so confirm you're on the right one if you run more than one.

steps.heading: Check your Balances page
steps.body: Head to Balances from the left-hand menu. This page shows your Incoming and Available totals and a Pay out button, and it's the same place you'll return to once Instant Payouts is active. A Setup guide panel on the right tracks whether you've finished the basic account steps: accepting payments, verifying your business, going live. All of it feeds into whether faster payout options are offered to you at all.

image.caption: The Balances page, with the Pay out control and a Setup guide checklist on the right tracking account completion.

steps.heading: Confirm your business details and country eligibility
steps.body:
Eligibility ties to your business profile and your account's country, not just your bank details. Check Settings > Business > Account details before assuming the feature is broken if it doesn't appear. Stripe wants your account name, business address, and related information complete and verified, since an incomplete profile is one of the quiet reasons this stays unavailable.

Instant Payouts also isn't offered everywhere Stripe operates. It covers around three dozen countries, including the US, UK, Canada, most of the EU, Australia and Singapore, but a Stripe account outside that list won't see the option regardless of how complete its profile is.

image.caption: The Business account details screen, where your account name and business address need to be complete and verified before some payout features unlock.

steps.heading: Read the eligibility and daily limit rules
steps.body:
New Stripe users aren't immediately eligible for Instant Payouts. Check eligibility directly on the Balances page or via the Balances API rather than assuming. Even once eligible, two separate caps apply each day: a maximum dollar amount, which you can see in the Dashboard, and a hard limit of 10 Instant Payouts per day regardless of amount.

Both caps reset at a fixed local time by region: midnight US Central Time for the US and Canada, midnight London time for the UK, midnight Paris time across the EU, and similar regional cutoffs elsewhere. A payout requested a few minutes before that reset still counts toward the prior day's limit.

image.caption: Stripe's documentation page on Instant Payouts eligibility, listing the daily reset time for each supported region.

steps.heading: Know the fee and the per-payout minimum and maximum
steps.body:
Instant Payouts aren't free. Stripe takes 1% in Canada, the EU, UK, Singapore, Norway, Hong Kong and Malaysia, and 1.5% in the US, Australia, New Zealand and UAE, pre-deducted so the balance shown is what you'd actually receive. Each transfer also has a currency-specific floor and ceiling; in the US that's $0.50 minimum and $9,999 maximum per payout.

Save Instant Payouts for moments where the speed is worth paying for, like covering a same-day shortfall. For routine payroll or predictable expenses, a standard payout costs nothing extra and just takes longer.

steps.heading: Add a payout method, then trigger the transfer
steps.body:
In most supported countries the eligible method is a debit card, but a few, including the US, UK, EU, Sweden, Denmark, Australia, Singapore and Hong Kong, also accept certain bank accounts. You only need to add a method once; until it's added and verified, the Balances page offers only your standard payout schedule.

Once it's in place, go to Balances and click Pay out. If you're eligible and have a positive balance, choose Instant, enter the amount, pick which balance to draw from and which method to pay out to, then click Review. The dashboard shows the fee and arrival time before you confirm.

troubleshooting.problem: The instant-available balance shows less than expected, or zero
troubleshooting.cause: Card payment funds count toward Instant Payouts as soon as the charge completes, but funds from ACH or other bank debits only count after they fully settle.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for bank-debit funds to settle, or check the instant_available field on the Balances API to see exactly what currently qualifies.

troubleshooting.problem: Can't request another Instant Payout today
troubleshooting.cause: The account hit its daily cap: a maximum dollar amount, or the flat limit of 10 Instant Payouts per day, whichever comes first.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the regional reset time, or use a standard payout for anything beyond the cap.

troubleshooting.problem: No debit card option appears when adding a payout method
troubleshooting.cause: A few countries, such as Hong Kong, support only certain bank accounts for Instant Payouts, not debit cards.
troubleshooting.fix: Add a supported bank account instead, and check Stripe's list of supported banks for that country.

faq.question: How fast are Stripe Instant Payouts?
faq.answer: Funds typically settle within 30 minutes of the request, rather than the several business days a standard payout can take.

faq.question: What's the exact fee?
faq.answer: 1% in Canada, the EU, UK, Singapore, Norway, Hong Kong and Malaysia. 1.5% in the US, Australia, New Zealand and UAE. It's deducted from the payout itself.

faq.question: Is there a minimum or maximum amount per payout?
faq.answer: Yes, and it's currency-specific. In the US it's $0.50 minimum and $9,999 maximum per Instant Payout.

faq.question: Is there a daily limit?
faq.answer: Two: a maximum total dollar amount for the day, and a separate hard cap of 10 Instant Payouts per day. Both reset at a fixed local time for your region.

faq.question: Does Instant Payout always land on a debit card?
faq.answer: Not always. Most supported countries require a debit card, but a handful, including the US, UK, EU, Sweden, Denmark, Australia, Singapore and Hong Kong, also accept certain bank accounts.

faq.question: Is Instant Payouts available in every country Stripe supports?
faq.answer: No. It's limited to roughly three dozen countries. A Stripe account outside that list won't see the option even with a fully verified profile.

faq.question: Why does my instant-available balance not match my full balance?
faq.answer: Funds from bank debits like ACH only count once they've settled, since they can still be reversed before that. Card payment funds are available immediately.
